# InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management

## Abstract

InfiniGen is a KV cache management framework that improves performance and accuracy in long-text generation by pre-fetching essential KV cache entries in offloading-based LLM serving systems. [...] generation, which synergistically works with modern offloading-based inference
systems. InfiniGen leverages the key insight that a few important tokens that
are essential for computing the subsequent attention layer in the Transformer
can be speculated by performing a minimal rehearsal with the inputs of the
current layer and part of the query weight and key cache of the subsequent
layer. This allows us to prefetch only the essential KV cache entries (without [...] fetching them all), thereby mitigating the fetch overhead from the host memory
in offloading-based LLM serving systems. Our evaluation on several
representative LLMs shows that InfiniGen improves the overall performance of a
modern offloading-based system by up to 3.00x compared to prior KV cache
management methods while offering substantially better model accuracy.

## AI Overview

When an LLM generates long text, it stores keys and values from earlier tokens so it need not recompute them. This store is the KV cache, and it grows with sequence length and batch size. Offloading the cache from GPU to larger CPU memory helps fit the workload. However, fetching it back over the CPU–GPU connection can become a major inference cost. [...] works with modern offloading-based inference systems. InfiniGen leverages the key insight that a few important tokens that are essential for computing the subsequent attention layer in the Transformer can be speculated by performing a minimal rehearsal with the inputs of the current layer and part of the query weight and key cache of the subsequent layer. This allows us to prefetch only the essential KV cache entries (without fetching them all), thereby mitigating the fetch overhead from the [...] overhead from the host memory in offloading-based LLM serving systems. Our evaluation on several representative LLMs shows that InfiniGen improves the overall performance of a modern offloading-based system by up to 3.00x compared to prior KV cache management methods while offering substantially better model accuracy.

Fast forward to today. KV cache is no longer an optimization at the margins of inference. It is the core infrastructure.

NVIDIA introduced ICMS (now renamed CMX) to formalize inference context storage. KV cache now represents the majority of the inference storage footprint. DRAM and SSD costs are becoming a significant line item in AI system budgets.

Loading Comments... [...] KV cache already departs from traditional caching in three fundamental ways.

First, it is persistent and multi-tier. It is stored across GPU, CPU, SSD, and cloud, survives beyond a single request, and is managed more like a data pipeline than a local buffer.

Second, it is not a black box. It can be compressed, quantized, and transformed. Its internal structure is exposed and exploitable by the systems that manage it.

KV Cache is an acceleration technology.It significantly improves the speed and efficiency of text generation by preserving important information from previous steps and reusing previously calculated results, avoiding recalculation each time. If the Large Language Model (LLM) is like a novelist, then the Transformer is his or her "thinking method." When a writer writes a story, he or she considers the previous content and decides what to write next.    Improved inference speed:Significantly reduces latency when generating long texts, improving the user experience.

This reduces the computational complexity of inference from quadratic to linear, significantly accelerating the process.
